name: South Africa
summary: Four national MNOs (Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, Telkom) plus Rain and Liquid. In ICASA's first spectrum auction (March 2022, R14.4bn) they bought 700, 800, 2600 and 3500 MHz. Legacy 900/1800/2100 assignments were rearranged under the 2022 RFSAPs. The next auction (750/800 MHz, 1.5, 2.3, 3.3, 3.5 GHz) is planned for the 2026/27 financial year.

operators.name: Vodacom
operators.notes: Vodafone Group subsidiary. Legacy spectrum is tied to its operating licence (expires 2029, per Vodafone 20-F); 2022-auction spectrum runs to 2042. Vodacom took a stake in fibre company Maziv (shown as an associate in Vodafone's FY26 20-F); that deal involves no spectrum.

operators.name: MTN
operators.notes: ICASA approved spectrum pooling with Liquid (1800 MHz) and with Cell C (900/1800/2100 MHz) in June 2022. Vodacom challenged this in the Gauteng High Court (ZAGPPHC 2025/199). Pooled spectrum is shown under each licensee.

operators.name: Cell C
operators.notes: Runs mostly on MTN's (and Vodacom's) networks through roaming and pooling agreements. In the 2022 auction it won 10 MHz at 3.5 GHz; the MTN affidavit (2024) says this assignment was then under dispute.

operators.name: Rain
operators.notes: Formerly WBS/iBurst. Holds 700, 1800, 2600 and 3.6 GHz spectrum. Uses Vodacom's infrastructure through a roaming/sharing arrangement.

operators.name: Liquid
operators.notes: Formerly Neotel. Its 1800 MHz spectrum is pooled with MTN's.

bands.label: 600 MHz
bands.note: Not an IMT band in South Africa. 470–694 MHz is kept for terrestrial broadcasting (DTT) under ICASA's RFSAP.

bands.label: 700 MHz FDD (IMT700)
bands.note: Auctioned in March 2022 (lots of 2×10 MHz); licences effective 1 July 2022, valid to 2042. Only 40 MHz (2×20) of the band was offered (MTN affidavit, para 43), and 703–713/758–768 MHz stays unassigned. Block positions come from spectrum-tracker.com only; the amounts match ICASA's results table.

blocks.notes: Opt-in stage 2022 (2×10 MHz for R1.15bn together with its 2600 lot)

bands.label: 733–758 MHz (IMT750 centre gap)
bands.note: Not yet assigned. ICASA has a final RFSAP for 733–758 MHz; the next IMT auction (2026/27 financial year) may include '750 MHz' (TechCentral, Feb 2026).

bands.label: 800 MHz FDD (IMT800)
bands.note: Auctioned in 2022: three lots of 2×10 MHz. One lot went unsold and ICASA says it will license it later; the next auction may include 800 MHz. Block positions come from spectrum-tracker.com only.

bands.label: 850 MHz (IMT850, 825–830 / 870–875 MHz)
bands.note: Legacy Neotel/Liquid CDMA assignment at 827.775–832.695 / 872.775–877.695 MHz. ICASA's IMT850 RFSAP moves it to 825–830 / 870–875 MHz and ends CDMA with the analogue TV switch-off. Current use and licensee could not be verified; spectrum-tracker.com still lists Liquid at 827.7–832.7 / 872.7–877.7 MHz.

bands.label: 900 MHz (IMT900)
bands.note: Positions follow ICASA's final IMT900 RFSAP (Government Gazette 47788, 20 Dec 2022, Figure 3 'Assignments from 1st April 2023'). The in-band migration finished by 31 March 2024 (MTN affidavit, para 52). 900–905 / 945–950 MHz is 'to be assigned separately' through an ITA. Vodafone's FY26 20-F lists Vodacom as '2×11' here, but that likely includes a footnote marker; ICASA's plan gives 2×10.

blocks.notes: To be assigned via a separate ITA

bands.label: 1.4/1.5 GHz L-band
bands.note: Not assigned. ICASA has a final IMT1500 assignment plan, and the next auction (2026/27) may include 1.5 GHz.

bands.label: AWS 1.7/2.1 GHz
bands.note: Not harmonised in ITU Region 1. 1710–1785 MHz is used as the B3 uplink.

bands.label: 1800 MHz (IMT1800)
bands.note: Six assignments of about 2×12 MHz, with small (~200 kHz) guard bands left between them (MTN affidavit, paras 49–53). MTN's block is 1722.7–1734.7 / 1817.7–1829.7 MHz (Gauteng High Court judgment, 2025). MTN pools its block with Liquid's adjacent block (one 20 MHz LTE carrier). Vodacom and Rain hold adjacent blocks.

holdings.notes: ICASA pooling approval letter refers to Liquid's and MTN's '2×12 MHz' in IMT1800
2×12 MHz from background knowledge, not source-verified. The pooling approval confirms Cell C holds 1800 MHz spectrum.

bands.label: PCS 1900 / 2 GHz MSS
bands.note: PCS 1900 is not used in Region 1. The 2 GHz MSS band (1980–2010/2170–2200) is not assigned for terrestrial IMT.

bands.label: 1900–1920 MHz TDD
bands.note: Unpaired 2 GHz spectrum was historically part of the 3G licences. Vodafone's FY26 20-F says ICASA approved Vodacom's 2100 MHz licence amendment returning its 2100 TDD spectrum. Other holders are not verified.

bands.label: 2100 MHz (IMT2100)
bands.note: Four 2×15 MHz assignments. MTN is at 1950–1965 / 2140–2155 MHz (court judgment). Cell C's block is adjacent and pooled with MTN's into one 20 MHz LTE carrier (MTN affidavit Figure 5, '15 MHz + 15 MHz').

holdings.notes: Telkom's 2100 amount is from background knowledge, not source-verified

bands.label: 2300 MHz (IMT2300)
bands.note: ICASA's final RFSAP makes 2300–2400 MHz exclusive to IMT TDD, with fixed links cleared by 31 March 2023. Unassigned spectrum is to go out through an ITA; the next auction may include 2.3 GHz. Telkom is believed (from background knowledge, not source-verified) to hold part of the band for TD-LTE. Existing holdings could not be verified.

bands.label: 2600 MHz FDD (IMT2600)
bands.note: The whole 2×70 MHz FDD block (140 MHz, MTN affidavit para 43) was sold in the 2022 auction. ICASA's results table counts both directions: Vodacom 80, MTN 40, Rain 20 MHz. Licences run to 2042. Block positions are not published.

holdings.notes: '80 MHz' in ICASA's results and Vodafone 20-F; Vodacom's largest contiguous assignment

bands.label: 2570–2620 MHz TDD centre gap
bands.note: Not part of the 2022 auction. WBS (now Rain) historically held 2550–2565 MHz, and the 2015 RFSAP moved it out. Current use of the centre gap is not verified.

bands.label: 3400–3600 MHz (IMT3500)
bands.note: ICASA's RFSAP converted the existing licences (Telkom, Liquid) from FDD to TDD and made the assignments contiguous. 86 MHz was sold in 2022. Positions are not published. Total shown: 114 MHz of 200 MHz. Liquid's pre-2022 holding is not included because its size could not be verified.

holdings.notes: 28 MHz held before 2022 (MTN affidavit) + 22 MHz won in 2022
Won in 2022; described as 'under dispute' in MTN's 2024 affidavit
2022 auction lot only; legacy holding not verified

bands.label: 3600–3800 MHz (3.6 GHz)
bands.note: Rain holds 3.6 GHz spectrum inherited from WBS (Wikipedia/Rain), used for its 5G FWA network. The amount and edges are not verified.

bands.label: 3300–3400 MHz (IMT3300)
bands.note: Not assigned. The final RFSAP took effect on 1 April 2023, and ICASA's next auction (2026/27) may include 3.3 GHz.

bands.label: 4.4–5.0 GHz
bands.note: No IMT assignment, and the band is not in ICASA's planned auctions.

bands.label: 6 GHz
bands.note: No IMT licences. ICASA plans dynamic spectrum access in 5925–6425 MHz. Whether upper 6 GHz goes to IMT or Wi-Fi was still open in 2026 (TechCentral).

bands.label: 26 GHz
bands.note: Not assigned. ICASA's IMT Roadmap 2026 proposes exclusive geographic areas for 24.25–27.5 GHz; no ITA has been issued.

bands.label: 37–43.5 GHz
bands.note: Not assigned. It is in the IMT Roadmap 2026 (37.5–43.5 GHz) with no ITA yet.

bands.label: 47 GHz
bands.note: Not assigned. It is in the IMT Roadmap 2026 (47.2–48.2 GHz) with no ITA yet.

notes: ICASA's March 2022 results table gives both directions for paired bands (e.g. '20 MHz' = 2×10 MHz). Holdings here are stored per direction.
Only 900 MHz has regulator-published block positions (ICASA RFSAP, Dec 2022). The 700/800 MHz positions come from spectrum-tracker.com alone and are marked unverified.
MTN's affidavit (2024) says Vodacom held 184 MHz and MTN 174 MHz of IMT spectrum. The holdings here give exactly these totals: Vodacom 20+20+24+30+80+10 and MTN 20+20+24+30+40+40.

Vodafone's FY26 20-F shows Vodacom's 900 MHz as '2×118 (2029)', read here as 2×11 with a footnote marker. ICASA's final IMT900 RFSAP gives each incumbent 2×10 MHz after migration, and that matches the affidavit totals, so 2×10 is used.

Spectrum pooling: MTN+Liquid (1800 MHz) and MTN+Cell C (900/1800/2100 MHz) were approved by ICASA on 21 June 2022. Vodacom's High Court challenge was decided in February 2025 (ZAGPPHC 2025/199); the outcome was not verified here.
As of 2026-09-28 no new IMT auction has been held. ICASA was still appointing auction advisers in February 2026 and aims to auction in FY2026/27.
Coverage badge lowered from "Holdings only" to "Partial" by the atlas-wide rule (block-level = every counted band verified; positions verified ≥ 60%; partial = a required band's status is unknown).

2100 MHz: Telkom's 2×15 MHz is not source-verified. Only MTN's block edges are known.
2300 MHz: Telkom's (and any other) holdings not verified.
3.5 GHz: Liquid's pre-2022 holding and all block positions are unknown. The status of Cell C's disputed 10 MHz is unverified.
3.6 GHz: Rain's amount and edges are unknown.
850 MHz: the current status of Liquid's legacy CDMA assignment is unknown.
1900–1920 MHz TDD and the 2570–2620 MHz centre gap: holders unknown.
Outcome of Vodacom v ICASA (spectrum pooling) not verified.
